newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares set records on new foreign funds.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares set records on new foreign funds.

text.p: Leading Russian shares opened at another record high on Wednesday, and traders said the market was set to rise further as new foreign investment continued to pour in.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose to 413.01, a 0.17 percent rise on Tuesday's close of 412.32.

"It is a crazy market -- new records are being set again this morning," said Brunswick director Martin Diggle. "There is an overwhelming flow of funds and there's simply not enough supply of stock to satisfy demand."
Oil company LUKoil which market operators say is making up for lagging the rest of the "blue chip" market earlier in the year, shot up to $21.00 at 0824 GMT from Tuesday's close of $18.71.
National power company UES also hit a new high, traders said, jumping to $0.3650 from $0.3535. Regional power company Mosenergo rose to $1.505 from $1.475.
But traders said not all stocks were at historic levels and saw the market powering higher by the end of the trading session despite some profit-taking by Russian players.
"It's probably worth noting that not everything is at an all-time high, but it will interesting to see whether they get there today," said Rinaco-Plus trader Tom Brackenbury.
"We have seen some local profit-takers but they are eclipsed by the size of foreign demand."
